title: Ankhorage Permissions
summary: Provides a platform-neutral permission registry and request/check helpers for Expo, React Native, React Native Web, and test environments.
purpose: Give applications a single typed boundary for declaring, checking, and requesting supported device and browser permissions without coupling their core code to a platform SDK.
responsibilities: Define the supported permission identifiers, states, and platform-neutral registry metadata.
Expose permission-manager, React, Expo, web, CLI, testing, and capability entrypoints.
Translate host-provided permission responses into consistent permission states.
boundaries: Does not directly select, install, or configure a browser, Expo, or React Native permission provider.
Does not determine product authorization policy after a platform permission is granted.
Does not persist application permission decisions or user data.
audience: Application authors supporting browser, Expo, React Native, or test permission flows.
Adapter authors that provide platform-specific permission clients.
useCases: Check or request camera, microphone, media-library, location, notification, or clipboard access.
Render consistent permission state in React applications.
Inspect supported permissions and required manifest metadata through the package capability provider.

architecture.role: Reusable cross-platform permission boundary with platform adapters at explicit Expo and web entrypoints.
invariants: The canonical permission registry remains platform-neutral.
Platform-specific APIs are isolated behind explicit client and adapter boundaries.
Consumers use published package entrypoints and declared dependencies.

limitations: Permission availability and final grant decisions remain controlled by the host platform and user.
Only permissions represented by the package registry can be checked or requested through its typed APIs.
